app.name: Renovate
nav.label: Main navigation
overview.title: Overview
overview.status.next: Everything is up to date. Next automatic run {when}.
overview.status.manual: Automatic runs are switched off. Start a run when you like.
overview.preview_hint: Looks for updates without changing anything in your repositories.
overview.preview_started: Preview started. Nothing will be changed.
overview.empty.title: Keep your dependencies up to date, automatically
overview.empty.text: Renovate watches your repositories and opens pull requests when a new version of something you use is available. Connect your git server to begin.
overview.empty.connect.title: Connect your server
overview.empty.connect.text: GitHub, GitLab, Gitea or Forgejo. Takes about a minute.
overview.empty.choose.title: Choose repositories
overview.empty.choose.text: Switch on the ones Renovate should look after.
overview.empty.review.title: Review the pull requests
overview.empty.review.text: You decide what gets merged. Nothing changes without your review.
connections.title: Connections
connections.subtitle: The git servers and accounts Renovate works with.
connections.empty.title: No connection yet
connections.empty.text: Connect GitHub, GitLab, Gitea or Forgejo to get started.
connections.managed_hint: This connection is defined in the app configuration. Change it there; the interface shows it read-only.
connections.sync_failed: Repository list could not be refreshed
connections.sync_error: The last refresh of the repository list failed: {message}
connections.name: Name
connections.enabled_hint: Switch off to pause the connection without losing its settings.
connections.mode.all: automatically: everything I can push to
connections.mode_hint: By hand: only repositories you switch on. Automatically: all repositories of the account, including new ones, narrowed by the patterns below.
connections.filter_hint: Patterns only apply in automatic mode. They match the full name, for example my-org/ha-*.
connections.include: Only these (one pattern per line, empty means all)
connections.patterns_hint: * matches within one folder name, ** matches across, ? matches one character.
connections.extra_hint: Renovate options in JSON that apply to every repository of this connection, for example {"labels": ["dependencies"]}. Options the app manages itself are refused.
connections.token_hint: Replace the token, for example when it expired. It must belong to the same account ({account}).
connections.token_name: The app created the token "{name}". Delete it in the settings of your server if you remove this connection.
connections.token_replaced_warning: Token replaced, but it lacks some permissions
connections.remove_text: The connection and its run history are deleted. Pull requests that Renovate already opened stay where they are.
connections.remove_text_token: The connection and its run history are deleted. The token "{token}" stays valid on your server until you delete it there. Pull requests that Renovate already opened stay where they are.
repositories.mode_selected: Only the repositories you switch on are processed. New repositories stay off until you switch them on.
repositories.mode_all: All repositories you can push to are processed, including new ones. Use the switches to exclude single ones, or the patterns in the settings.
repositories.col.name: Repository
wizard.title: Connect a git server
wizard.subtitle: Four short steps. You can change everything later.
wizard.provider.gitea: Your own Gitea, also the Home Assistant app
wizard.self_hosted.gitea: My server uses a different address
wizard.self_hosted.forgejo: My server uses a different address
wizard.address_hint: The address you open in the browser. The API path is added automatically.
wizard.discovered: Found a Gitea in Home Assistant: {url} (version {version}).
wizard.device.explain: You get a short code and confirm it on {name}. No password and no token to copy.
wizard.password.explain: Enter your {name} login once. The app creates an access token with just the permissions Renovate needs. Your password is not stored.
wizard.token.step1.github: Click the button below. GitHub opens with the right permissions already selected.
wizard.token.step1.gitlab: Click the button below. GitLab opens with name and permissions already filled in.
wizard.token.step1.gitea: Click the button below to open your token settings. Create a new token there.
wizard.token.step1.forgejo: Click the button below to open your token settings. Create a new token there.
wizard.token.step2: Required permissions: {scopes}. Then create the token.
wizard.token.step3: Copy the token and paste it below. It is shown only once.
wizard.token.label: Token
wizard.verified_counts: {total} repositories found, {pushable} of them can be updated.
wizard.warning.missing_scope: The token lacks the permission "{scope}". Some updates will fail until you add it.
wizard.no_pushable: This account cannot push to any repository. Renovate needs write access to open pull requests.
wizard.name: Name of this connection
wizard.name_hint: Only for you, to tell connections apart.
wizard.repositories.title: Which repositories should Renovate look after?
wizard.repositories.text: Start with a few. Renovate opens a "Configure Renovate" pull request in repositories that have no configuration yet; nothing is changed before you merge it.
wizard.done.title: All set
wizard.done.text: Start with a preview: Renovate looks for updates and shows what it would do, without changing anything.
wizard.done.onboarding: After a real run you will find a "Configure Renovate" pull request in repositories that are new to Renovate. Merge it to switch Renovate on there.
runs.title: Runs
runs.subtitle: Every time Renovate looked at your repositories.
runs.empty.title: No runs yet
runs.empty.text: Start one from the overview, or wait for the schedule.
runs.branch.already-existed: Pull request is up to date
runs.branch.pr-limit-reached: Limit of open pull requests reached
runs.branch.needs-approval: Needs your approval in the Dependency Dashboard
runs.branch.needs-pr-approval: Needs your approval in the Dependency Dashboard
runs.branch.pending: Waiting for the release to age
diagnosis.no_repositories: No repositories are switched on for this connection, so there was nothing to do. Switch some on in the connection.
diagnosis.authentication: The git server rejected the token. It may have expired or been revoked. Replace it in the settings of the connection.
diagnosis.network: The server could not be reached. Check the address of the connection and the network of Home Assistant.
diagnosis.tls: The certificate of the server is not trusted. Provide your CA certificate in the app configuration (Advanced).
diagnosis.rate_limit: The server limits how often it can be asked. Add a token for github.com in the settings (Renovate), or run less often.
diagnosis.out_of_memory: Renovate ran out of memory. Choose the Light profile, lower the number of repositories per batch, or give each run more memory in the settings (Resources).
diagnosis.disk_full: The disk is full. Clear the cache in the settings (Maintenance) or free up space.
diagnosis.timeout: The run took longer than the time limit and was stopped. Raise the limit in the settings (Resources) or process fewer repositories per run.
diagnosis.failed: Renovate stopped with an error. The log below shows details.
webhooks.explain: With webhooks the git server tells the app when something happens, for example when you merge a pull request, so Renovate reacts within a minute instead of waiting for the next scheduled run. Your server must be able to reach this app from outside.
webhooks.no_url: Enter the public address of the webhook port first.
webhooks.port: The app listens on port {port}. Make it reachable in the network settings of the app.
webhooks.register: Set up in all switched-on repositories
settings.title: Settings
settings.subtitle: Changes are saved as you make them.
settings.how_it_works: Settings with a lock are fixed in the app configuration (Settings → Apps → Renovate → Configuration). Everything else you change here.
settings.resources.limits: {runs} parallel run(s), {memory} MB per run, {batch} repositories per batch, CPU priority {priority}
settings.resources.machine: This machine: {memory} MB memory, {cpus} CPU cores
settings.maintenance.title: Maintenance
settings.maintenance.text: Renovate keeps a cache of package information to run faster. Old runs are removed automatically.
settings.maintenance.clear_cache_text: The next run takes longer because the cache is built again.
settings.group.resources.help: How much of this machine a run may use. The automatic profile fits the memory of your system.
settings.group.history.help: How long runs and their logs are kept.
settings.group.renovate.help: Defaults for all repositories. A renovate.json in a repository can override most of them.
settings.group.webhooks.help: Let the git server trigger runs when something happens.
settings.group.home_assistant.help: What the app reports to Home Assistant.
settings.group.advanced.help: For special setups: certificates, extra tools, environment variables.
settings.general.language.label: Language
settings.general.theme.label: Theme
settings.general.theme.help: Auto follows Home Assistant, then your system.
settings.general.accent.label: Accent color
settings.general.accent.help: Blue is the default. Home Assistant uses the primary color of your Home Assistant theme.
settings.general.accent_color.label: Custom accent color
settings.general.accent_color.help: Used when the accent color is set to Custom. Format #RRGGBB.
settings.general.log_level.label: Log level of the app
settings.general.log_level.help: How much the app writes to its log. Renovate's own detail level is set under Advanced.
settings.general.timezone.label: Time zone
settings.general.timezone.help: Used for the schedule, for example Europe/Berlin. Empty uses the time zone of Home Assistant.
settings.schedule.mode.label: Automatic runs
settings.schedule.mode.help: Cron uses a schedule, interval repeats after a fixed time, manual never starts by itself.
settings.schedule.cron.label: Cron schedule
settings.schedule.cron.help: Five fields: minute hour day month weekday. 0 */6 * * * means every six hours.
settings.schedule.interval_minutes.label: Interval (minutes)
settings.schedule.interval_minutes.help: Used when automatic runs are set to Interval.
settings.schedule.run_on_start.label: Run when the app starts
settings.schedule.run_on_start.help: Start a run a moment after the app started.
settings.resources.profile.label: Resource profile
settings.resources.profile.help: Light for a Raspberry Pi, Balanced for most systems, Performance for strong machines. Automatic chooses by memory.
settings.resources.max_concurrent_runs.h: How many connections are processed at the same time. Overrides the profile.
settings.resources.memory_limit_mb.label: Memory per run (MB)
settings.resources.memory_limit_mb.help: Upper limit for the memory of one Renovate process. Overrides the profile.
settings.resources.batch_size.label: Repositories per batch
settings.resources.batch_size.help: Renovate is restarted after this many repositories, which keeps memory low. Overrides the profile.
settings.resources.cpu_priority.label: CPU niceness
settings.resources.cpu_priority.help: 0 is normal, 19 is the most considerate. Higher values keep Home Assistant responsive. Overrides the profile.
settings.resources.run_timeout_minutes.h: A run that takes longer is stopped.
settings.history.keep_runs.label: Runs to keep
settings.history.keep_log_days.label: Days to keep logs
settings.history.keep_log_days.help: Runs older than this are removed with their logs.
settings.renovate.dry_run.label: Dry run
settings.renovate.dry_run.help: Off makes real changes. The other modes only look: extract finds dependencies, lookup also checks for updates, full simulates everything.
settings.renovate.onboarding.label: Onboarding pull request
settings.renovate.onboarding.help: Open a "Configure Renovate" pull request in repositories without configuration. Off means Renovate needs no configuration, see below.
settings.renovate.onboarding_preset.help: The preset written into the onboarding pull request.
settings.renovate.require_config.label: Configuration file
settings.renovate.require_config.help: Required: only repositories with a configuration are processed. Optional: repositories without one are processed with defaults. Ignored: repository files are not read.
settings.renovate.git_author.label: Commit author
settings.renovate.git_author.help: Name and address of the commits, as Name <address>. Empty uses Renovate's default.
settings.renovate.default_extends.label: Default presets
settings.renovate.default_extends.help: Presets applied to every repository, for example group:allNonMajor.
settings.renovate.default_labels.label: Default labels
settings.renovate.default_labels.help: Labels added to every pull request.
settings.renovate.pr_concurrent_limit.he: Maximum per repository. 0 means no limit. Empty uses Renovate's default.
settings.renovate.pr_hourly_limit.label: New pull requests per hour
settings.renovate.pr_hourly_limit.help: Maximum per repository. 0 means no limit. Empty uses Renovate's default.
settings.renovate.github_com_token.label: Token for github.com
settings.renovate.github_com_token.help: Lets Renovate read release notes and changelogs from GitHub without hitting rate limits. A token without any permissions is enough.
settings.renovate.host_rules.label: Credentials for registries
settings.renovate.host_rules.help: Logins for private package sources such as a Docker registry or an npm proxy.
settings.renovate.config_file.label: Configuration file in the app folder
settings.renovate.config_file.help: A JSON file with Renovate options, placed in the app's configuration folder (addon_configs). Merged over the defaults above.
settings.webhooks.enabled.label: Receive webhooks
settings.webhooks.enabled.help: Opens a port that git servers can send events to.
settings.webhooks.port.label: Port
settings.webhooks.port.help: Also enable this port in the network settings of the app.
settings.webhooks.public_url.label: Public address
settings.webhooks.public_url.help: The address your git server uses to reach the port, for example https://hooks.example.org. Without it, webhooks cannot be set up automatically.
settings.webhooks.debounce_seconds.label: Wait before running (seconds)
settings.webhooks.debounce_seconds.help: Events within this time are combined into one run.
settings.webhooks.ignore_own_events.help: Prevents Renovate's own pull requests from starting new runs in a loop.
settings.home_assistant.sensors.label: Sensors
settings.home_assistant.events.label: Events
settings.home_assistant.events.help: Fires the event renovate_run_finished after every run, for automations.
settings.home_assistant.failure_notifica: Shows a notification in Home Assistant when a run fails.
settings.advanced.renovate_log_level.hel: Detail level of the run logs. Debug is very verbose.
settings.advanced.extra_packages.label: Extra system packages
settings.advanced.extra_packages.help: Alpine packages installed when the app starts, for example python3, py3-pip or go. Needed when Renovate has to run those tools to update lock files.
settings.advanced.extra_env.label: Extra environment variables
settings.advanced.extra_env.help: Passed to every Renovate run, for example proxy or registry settings.
settings.advanced.ca_certificate.label: CA certificate
settings.advanced.ca_certificate.help: File name of a certificate authority in /ssl or in the app folder. Needed for servers with a self-made certificate.
settings.advanced.insecure_tls.label: Do not verify certificates
settings.advanced.insecure_tls.help: Accepts any certificate. Insecure: prefer providing the CA certificate.
settings.advanced.github_client_id.label: GitHub OAuth client ID
settings.advanced.github_client_id.help: Use your own GitHub OAuth app (with device flow enabled) for the sign-in with a code.
settings.advanced.extra_env.field.name: Name
error.provider_unauthorized: The server rejected the token. Check that it is correct and has not expired.
error.provider_forbidden: The server denied access. The token probably lacks permissions.
error.provider_not_found: The server answered, but not like a git server. Check the address.
error.provider_unreachable: The server cannot be reached. Check the address and that the server is running.
error.provider_tls: The certificate of the server is not trusted. Provide your CA certificate in the app configuration (Advanced).
error.provider_rate_limited: The server is limiting requests. Try again in a few minutes.
error.provider_error: The server reported an error. Try again later.
error.provider_otp_required: This account uses two-factor authentication. Enter the current code.
error.invalid_address: That address does not look right. Use something like https://git.example.org.
error.expired: This step has expired. Please start again.
error.invalid_name: The name may contain letters, digits, spaces and . _ ( ) -
error.name_taken: A connection with this name already exists.
error.connection_managed: This connection is defined in the app configuration and cannot be changed here.
error.account_mismatch: The token belongs to a different account than this connection.
error.setting_locked: This setting is fixed in the app configuration.
error.nothing_to_run: No connection has repositories switched on yet.
error.webhooks_not_ready: Switch on webhooks and enter the public address first.
error.forbidden_source: This interface is only reachable through Home Assistant.
error.internal_error: Something went wrong. See the app log for details.
wizard.warning.missing_profile: The account has no full name or email address in its profile. Renovate uses them for its commits, so add them in your server's account settings.
config.problems_text: These entries could not be applied. Fix them in the app configuration; it is picked up within seconds.
chip.restart_hint: The app configuration changed extra packages or certificates. They are only applied when the app starts.
settings.config.title: App configuration
settings.config.text: Changes saved in the app configuration are picked up within seconds, without a restart. Only extra system packages and certificates need a restart of the app.
settings.config.unchanged: The app configuration is already up to date
error.oauth_expired: The sign-in through the browser can no longer be renewed. Sign in again by adding the connection anew.
error.oauth_missing_code: The address does not contain a code. Paste the whole address of the page that opened after the sign-in.
error.oauth_state_mismatch: This address belongs to another sign-in. Start again.
error.oauth_failed: The server did not return an access token. Check the client ID and that the application is registered as a public client.
error.webhooks_unsupported: Webhooks are not available for this server type.
error.client_id_required: Please enter the client ID of the application.
wizard.beta_hint: This server type is new. It was built from the documentation without a real server to test against, so please report what does not work.
wizard.provider.bitbucket-server: Your own Bitbucket Server or Data Center
wizard.token.step1.bitbucket: Click the button below to open your Atlassian API tokens and create a token with the Bitbucket permissions.
wizard.token.step1.bitbucket-server: Click the button below to open the HTTP access tokens of your account and create one.
wizard.token.step1.azure: Click the button below to open your personal access tokens and create one.
wizard.token.step1.gerrit: Click the button below to open the HTTP credentials of your Gerrit account and generate a password.
wizard.token.step1.scm-manager: Click the button below to open your API keys in SCM-Manager and create one.
wizard.token.step2_none: No special permissions are needed here. The account must be allowed to push branches and open pull requests.
wizard.username.hint.bitbucket: The user name of the account. If Bitbucket asks for the email address of your Atlassian account with API tokens, use that.
wizard.username.hint.gerrit: The user name of the Gerrit account the HTTP password belongs to.
wizard.browser.explain: You sign in on the page of {name} itself, so a passkey, a YubiKey or single sign-on works exactly as it does there. The app never sees your password.
wizard.browser.register_text: Open the application settings and create an OAuth2 application with these values:
wizard.browser.value_public: Confidential client: switch off (a public client, no secret)
wizard.browser.client_id_hint: Shown by the server after you saved the application.
wizard.browser.after: After you approve, the browser shows an error page (it tries to open 127.0.0.1). That is expected. Copy the address of that page from the address bar and paste it below.
wizard.browser.paste: Address of the page after the sign-in
wizard.browser.renews: The access token expires after a short time. The app renews it automatically before every run.
connections.browser_login: This connection is signed in through the browser. Its token is renewed automatically.
connections.browser_login_again: To sign in again, for example after the sign-in was revoked, add the connection anew.
webhooks.unsupported: {name} connections cannot use webhooks. The schedule starts the runs.
diagnosis.oauth_expired: The sign-in through the browser can no longer be renewed (revoked or expired). Add the connection anew to sign in again.
